details:
Earth Jukebox turns NASA Earth-observation imagery into sound, so that Earth data can be explored by listening as well as by looking.

WHAT IT DOES
A reading line sweeps a fixed world map from west to east. For every longitude, the app reads the data values under the line and plays them as a soft musical texture: latitude sets the pitch (on a pentatonic scale, so it stays musical), and the data value shapes loudness and timbre. A "What you hear" panel shows, for the current column, the real values at several latitudes, the notes being played and a latitude profile chart, so the sound is always explained by the data behind it.

Eight NASA layers act as instruments: sea surface temperature, precipitation rate, sea ice concentration, vegetation (NDVI), ocean chlorophyll-a, water vapor, cloud optical thickness and night-time lights. Users can mix layers, mute or solo them, and choose scenes (Ocean, Land & Life, Sky/Poles, Ocean Life, Humans, Air & Clouds, Everything).

TIME TRAVEL
A date picker (default: the latest complete day) lets people hear Earth on any day for which data exists. "Then vs Now" and "This day in history" compare the same calendar day in different years. Each layer card shows the requested date and the date actually used. If no observation exists within a product's own time resolution, the layer says "Not available" and stays silent instead of inventing data. Sea ice for recent dates is shown from the latest archive year and labeled "Archive". A share link stores the date, scene and active layers.

HOW IT WORKS
A global 1440x720 image of each layer is requested from NASA GIBS (WMS, EPSG:4326) and drawn on a canvas. Each pixel's color is decoded back into a data value using the layer's official GIBS colormap. For each column the app smooths neighboring pixels, maps latitude to pitch and the value to loudness and timbre, and synthesizes the sound in the browser with the Web Audio API. Everything runs in the browser; there is no back end.

LIMITS
Values are colormap-bin midpoint estimates, so they are not more precise than the colormap itself. Layers with satellite gaps or land/ice masks are silent where there is no reading.

TOOLS
TypeScript, Vite, Web Audio API, NASA GIBS (WMS), Vercel (hosting), GitHub.
